print_policy.purpose: A learner or a teacher can print the page: a PDF icon in the fixed header opens the PDF printed from this very page, ready for the print dialog of the tablet.
print_policy.accessible_name: Open the PDF of this page to print it
print_policy.link_must_resolve: A page that links its PDF is published only with that PDF beside it, printed from the same bytes (print-receipt.json); a link that does not resolve refuses the publication.

standalone_policy.purpose: A learner page that did not come through render_core (a snapshot, a suite, a page written by hand or taken from another tool) meets the shell's own policies, read from its own bytes. The renderer meets them by construction; nothing else does unless something checks.

rules.statement: A page loads no script, stylesheet, font, image or frame from the network. A link to a source is a citation and is allowed; a dependency is not.
A page declares a viewport and never turns zoom off: no user-scalable=no, no maximum-scale under the limit.
No declared text size is under the learner text floor. A size that scaling changes (an SVG label in a narrow column) is measured by the browser audit.
Every relative reference lands on a file that exists, and every fragment on an id that page holds.
A reference that leaves the governed root means the page is not whole where it is shipped alone. Said, not held: whether it matters depends on what is shipped.
No control character in the source: a TeX escape read as one (\v for \vec, \f for \frac) is gone from the maths.
TeX in the visible text means a script on the page renders it; maths shown as raw delimiters is not maths.
Storage is read only inside a try block: with storage blocked the read throws, and one throw ends the script.
No configuration for a vendor script the page does not load: it throws on every load.
An id appears once on a page.

standalone_policy.ledger_rule: A page may have no more findings of a rule than the ledger records, and a page the ledger does not list has none. The ledger holds what was already there when the rule arrived; the checker writes it, and it can only be tightened.

measures: touch targets of at least 48 px
rendered text size, SVG labels included
browser_audit.note: These need a rendered page. A snapshot is not done until this audit has run on it; the static rules above are what a pull request can be held to without a browser.

levels.REQUIRED: The page is a gap while the component is absent or has fewer than min_items: the renderer records a typed gap that names the record to author, and the rendered-page gate fails the product.
levels.EXPECTED: A learner should see it. Its absence is an advisory that names the record field to author, never a silent omission, and never a reason to invent content.
levels.OPTIONAL: Shown when the record has it.

column.FULL: A band across the whole page width.
column.PRIMARY: The main column of the expanded two-column layout; in the compact flow it comes first.
column.SUPPORT: The support column of the expanded layout; it follows the primary column in the compact flow.

component_policy.waivers: A record may declare an EXPECTED component not applicable, with a written reason, in extensions['grade9v3:component_waivers'] as {COMPONENT_ID: reason}; the reason is kept in the page and the receipt. A REQUIRED component cannot be waived, and a page never waives anything itself.
component_policy.depth: min_items is the floor below which a component does not count as present. target_items is the depth of the reference page, and target_items_by_band gives it by the difficulty band the record declares at band_source (for a Core1A construction unit, the hardest band among the bank questions it names in crux_question_refs). Between the floor and the reference depth the renderer says so as an advisory.
component_policy.held_to: FLOOR: official records and products are judged at the floor; an EXPECTED component that is absent is an advisory. REFERENCE: new authoring (a TEST deploy, a scaffolded owner bank) is judged at the reference depth, and an EXPECTED component must be present or waived by the record; otherwise it is a gap.

coverage.purpose: A product shows what the library holds for its subject, not what an author happened to list: the list of selected questions is a choice, and a choice leaves a record.
coverage.denominator: What product_manifest.derive would select: for Core2, the exam-bank questions whose capability or concept bucket belongs to the package; for Core2A and Core2B, the package questions exposed to that Core.
coverage.rule: Every record of the denominator is selected, or omitted by the manifest with a reason (coverage.omitted: {record id: why}); the hardest question of the denominator, by the toughest-concept rule, is selected.
coverage.sources: Source documents whose questions the library does not hold as records yet are declared in the manifest (coverage.sources: source, kind, questions, ingested, status). They are counted and said on the page of Deployments and in the receipt; nothing is rendered from them, and the figures are the author's claim.

promotion.purpose: A record that its own status says is not ready to teach is not selected into a product.
promotion.note: A record that declares no status makes no claim and is not refused. What a selected record must contain is the blueprint's own components: a REQUIRED one that is absent is a gap, as before.

typeset.purpose: An equation a learner is meant to read is typeset, not left as the author's plain text.
typeset.rule: A relation shown on a page carries presentation MathML (relation.mathml, the restricted subset the renderer accepts). One that has only an expression is shown as plain text, and the build says so.

admission.purpose: A question record is admitted by the library's own intake and resolver. A registration does not bring a gate of its own: a gate that checks that fields are non-empty cannot see a record that says nothing.

points.statement: The stem asks something: it has at least 6 words and is not made of sentences that the record's own hints or solution also say.
The stem ends where a sentence ends; a stem cut off mid-sentence asks half a question. Said, not held: a stem that ends on a variable looks the same from the text.
An option carries text. A letter standing for itself ('(A) A') is a choice with nothing to choose.

A number a hint relies on is in the stem, the options or the conditions, so a learner who has not opened the hint can already start. Said, not held: a constant or a value worked out from the stem looks the same from the text.

The question does not teach a concept the scope document defers (read from Shared/policy/grade9-physics.v1.json; an entry that names a row of the scope document is held to it by a test), unless the record is routed as a declared extension. A concept only the policy defers is said, not held, until the document names it. A question that excludes the concept ('do not invent a torque equation') is not refused. The capability tag is not the test: the registrar writes it.

The answer is about this question: it shares at least 2 words or numbers with the stem, options and conditions. No list of banned phrases is kept; an answer that could stand under any question fails without one.
The answer is worked: at least 2 reasoning steps and 80 characters of reasoning, and a summary of at most 500 characters that states the result; a page pasted in as the summary is not a result.
A key that nobody ran (NOT_RUN), or that someone disputes, does not enter a library. The status is the author's word, so it is a floor and not a proof.

admission.note: Intake and the resolver stay the one gate of record: CI runs them over every committed library (tests/test_question_admission.py), and a registration does not bring a gate of its own. These sit beside the corpus checks that were already there (duplicated and templated text, unresolved references). A package intake refuses is not registered, whatever else is said about it. What none of this can do is tell a plausible wrong explanation from a right one; a numeric key computed from the stem's own givens by an oracle would. Each point and each page rule names the assurance type its evidence is of; a check that proves part of a type (a static page rule cannot prove a layout) feeds a type of its own and leaves the whole type open.

evidence.purpose: A digest is taken over the bytes of a file, so the bytes must be the same on every machine.
evidence.note: Text is LF in every working tree (`* text=auto eol=lf`). A file already committed with CRLF keeps its bytes, so no recorded digest moves; a new file is LF.

blueprints.learner_job: Orient to the bucket without replacing detailed teaching.
Preserve authentic assessment demand while allowing bounded, provenance-explicit help that advances the learner without becoming a Question Clinic.

authoring.hint: One sentence naming the wrong route learners take and why it tempts. It must not give the answer or the right route.

components.benchmark: selected_question_bank_TABLET_STUDY: the options cards; the commit step is this app's own attempt-first rule

components.purpose: Show the situation as a picture drawn only from what the question states; every question in the benchmark has one.
components.benchmark: selected_question_bank_TABLET_STUDY: the 'Representation' card with the question-aligned schematic

authoring.hint: Add a representation to the package with an authored SVG (role=img, aria-labelledby or aria-label, <title> and <desc>) drawn only from the question's own data (labels at least 14 units high in a viewBox no wider than 440 units, so they read on a tablet), then name its id in figure_refs. Every question gets one; a classification or a pure-number question can show the quantities as a labelled diagram. If a question truly has nothing to draw, say so in extensions['grade9v3:component_waivers'] with the reason.

components.purpose: Let the learner ask for help one rung at a time; every rung says what it is for and whose words it carries.
components.benchmark: selected_question_bank_TABLET_STUDY: 'Hint ladder · reveal only what you need', five rungs on a hard question (represent / first move, connect, crux, equation / formal model, assembly checkpoint) with SOURCE and EXPANSION pills

authoring.hint: Write scaffolds[], one rung per job, in the order a learner meets them: a D1 or D2 question needs 3 (REPRESENTATION, KEY_CONCEPT, CRUX), a D3 or D4 question 5 (then FORMAL_MODEL, which gives the relation to use, and CHECKPOINT, which gives an intermediate result to compare against). Each has text (the hint), prompt (a question that makes the learner do the step), support_kind (REPRESENT, CONNECT or EXECUTE), reveals (CONCEPT or METHOD; ANSWER is held back until the solution), learner_stage and supports_move_ref (the id of the move it prepares). A rung must teach something specific to this question and must not repeat another rung or state the answer. Delete the rungs the question's band does not need.

components.purpose: Send the learner back to the concept page for the idea the question uses.
components.benchmark: selected_question_bank_TABLET_STUDY: concept links beside the hints (the Core1A cross-link)

components.purpose: Open the full working only after an attempt.
components.benchmark: selected_question_bank_TABLET_STUDY: the 'Teacher solution · complete derivation' disclosure

components.purpose: Show the working as numbered moves: what is done, why it is valid, what it gives.
components.benchmark: selected_question_bank_TABLET_STUDY: three or four numbered steps with a bold lead and the reason (geometry, balance, Newton II, eliminate)

authoring.hint: Write answer.reasoning_route[]: 3 moves for a D1 or D2 question, 4 for a D3 or D4. Each move has id, kind (DECIDE, REPRESENT, CONNECT, TRANSFORM or VERIFY), action (what is done), why_valid (the physical or logical reason this step is allowed; not 'this follows from the model'), inputs and output. Set crux_move_ref to the id of the move a learner is most likely to miss. Delete the move the band does not need.

components.purpose: State the final answer in one place.
components.benchmark: selected_question_bank_TABLET_STUDY: the green answer box

components.purpose: Test the answer by a route the working did not use.
components.benchmark: selected_question_bank_TABLET_STUDY: the 'Check.' line under the answer

authoring.hint: One sentence that tests the result independently: a limiting case, a unit check or a special value.

components.benchmark: core1a-motion-in-a-plane-tablet: the concept-card header with number, decision and unit id

components.purpose: Name the one step learners cannot infer on their own.
components.benchmark: core1a-motion-in-a-plane-tablet: the inferential-leap banner

authoring.hint: inferential_jump: one or two sentences naming the step a learner does not make unaided and why it is not obvious.

components.purpose: Say what the learner must already hold and what model is assumed.
components.benchmark: core1a-motion-in-a-plane-tablet: the 'Model contract & assumptions' tile

authoring.hint: List in entry_assumptions[] each thing a learner must already be able to do before this concept, one per entry and specific to this concept.

components.purpose: Say which source question this unit builds toward and the move a learner most often misses in it, so the concept is taught for that question and not only named after it.
components.benchmark: core1a-motion-in-a-plane-tablet: each concept card is built around the inferential leap the practice questions need

authoring.hint: Write crux_question_refs on a construction unit: the ids of the bank questions whose crux the unit builds, and crux_step_ref: the one of its step_refs that builds the move those questions turn on (the page marks that step). The toughest question of the set (the deploy names it) must be named by a unit of the concept it belongs to; that unit's steps must lead to the move the question turns on, and its worked example is that question (bank_anchor_ref). A unit that only shares the question's topic does not build its crux, and a step that mentions the idea in passing is not the step that builds it: draw the whole idea (for a sum of two vectors, every angle and not only the right angle).

components.purpose: Build the idea in steps; every step says what is done, why it is valid and what state it gives.
components.benchmark: core1a-motion-in-a-plane-tablet: step cards (action, why physically valid, state output)

authoring.hint: Each construction unit lists step_refs naming 2 or more teaching_path steps; each step has action, why_valid and output written for this unit, none repeated from another unit. A unit that builds the crux of a D3 or D4 question (it names that question in crux_question_refs) needs 4 steps, and its last step is the move that question turns on.

components.purpose: Put the relations a unit uses beside their meaning and when they hold.

authoring.hint: Each construction unit names the microtopic's relations it uses in construction_units[].relation_refs; each relation record needs its expression, meaning and conditions. A subject that declares no gates writes gate_relation_ref: null.

components.purpose: Walk one authentic question through the construction.

Draw each unit's own picture; do not reuse one figure on many units. Draw it in a viewBox no wider than 440 units with every label at least 14 units high, so the labels read on a tablet.

Each statement is specific to the unit.

blueprints.learner_job: Elicit the conceptual decision before reconstruction, diagnosis and repair.
Teach a familiar application route with progressive support and complete closure.
Protect the changed decision before commitment, then provide transfer review and repair.

Test the tempting model of the hardest concept of the question set against a model that cannot be argued with, rebuild the mathematics from what is visible, find where it stops being true, and then do a fresh task without the explorer.

components.purpose: See the eleven steps of the route and which one the learner is on, so the page is a path with an end and not a toy.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): the mandatory cognitive sequence, one chip per step

components.purpose: Name the one concept the page is for, the tempting model it replaces, the move to acquire, what survives and where it stops: the toughest concept of the question set.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): one explorer, one cognitive target

authoring.hint: target: question_ref is the toughest question of the set (python3 Shared/tools/explorer_build.py new fills it in; python3 Shared/tools/toughest_concept.py MANIFEST names it). failure: the learner's tempting model, one sentence, in the learner's words. operation: the move to acquire. invariant: what survives every valid variation. boundary: where the shortcut stops being right. quantity: the id of the quantity the whole page is about.

components.purpose: Show the owner's question the concept comes from, word for word, so that the explorer rejoins it.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): the exit rejoins the same semantic leaf

components.purpose: The state the learner moves (sliders) and the givens that stay fixed: the only way the page changes.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): direct manipulation of one governed state

authoring.hint: parameters: each {id, label, unit, min, max, step, value} for a slider, or {id, label, unit, value, fixed: true} for a given of the question. max - min must be a whole number of steps and value a position of the slider. Ids are letters, digits and underscores (theta, v_1); never a word of the expression language (min, max, if, e, pi).

components.purpose: Every number the page shows, as an expression of the parameters, so each one is computed and none is typed.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): one authoritative state; no invented exact parameters

authoring.hint: quantities: in order, each {id, label, unit, expr, decimals}; expr uses the parameters and earlier quantities: + - * / ^ ( ), sqrt abs hypot min max clamp round if(c,a,b) sin cos tan (radians), sind cosd tand asind acosd atand atan2d (degrees), pi, and comparisons with and/or/not. Write 2*a*b, never 2ab; v_x is written as a subscript. Include the quantity the page is about, the tempting model's value, and the parts the mechanism shows.

components.purpose: The phenomenon and, one step at a time, its hidden mechanism, drawn from the model's own numbers; and the checks that tie the drawing to them.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): G1 phenomenon and G2 mechanism; rendered-geometry truth

authoring.hint: scene: title, job (what this view shows that the other cannot), description (what a learner who cannot see it is told), world {x:[min,max], y:[min,max]} (keep the aspect between 0.36 and 1.1), elements of kind point, segment, arrow, circle, arc, polygon, curve, text. Coordinates are expressions: at/from/to/center are [x, y]; curve has param, t_min, t_max, x, y. role: object, given, result, wrong (the tempting model, dashed), helper, frame. label may show a number as {quantity:decimals}. reveal: start (the situation), manipulate (the result), contradict (the tempting model), deconstruct (the mechanism: components, constraints, forces, relative motion). The check says where an element leaves the picture. oracles: expressions that tie the drawing to the quantities using an element's numbers (arrow_x1, arrow_y2, point_x, circle_r, arc_a2).

components.purpose: A second representation that does a different reasoning job from the picture: the quantity against the slider, with the tempting model's curve as a ghost.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): coordinated representations that add distinct reasoning value

authoring.hint: second_view: kind graph, title, job, description, x (a slider parameter), series [{quantity, label, role}] (include the quantity the page is about), guides [{expr, label, orient: h or v}] for bounds the learner should see, ghost {quantity, label} for the tempting model (drawn only at the contradiction).

components.purpose: Place the learner in the situation the question describes, with the question itself, before any equation or control.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): CONTEXT

authoring.hint: context.situation: one to three sentences placing the learner in the physical or geometric situation, with no equation and no hint of the answer.

components.purpose: The learner commits to a prediction before any control moves; the page keeps it and returns to it after the evidence.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): PREDICT; prediction occurs before answer reveal

authoring.hint: predict.prompt, predict.options (three): each {text, tests: [{set: {parameter: value}, holds: expression, says: sentence with {quantity:decimals}}]}. An option is true of the model when all its tests hold. Exactly one option is true (predict.correct is its index); every other has a test that fails, and says tells the learner what that test showed. Make the tempting wrong model one of the options. Expressions may read the whole model: at(R, theta, 90) is R with theta set to 90, maxover(R, theta) and minover(R, theta) its largest and smallest, argmax(R, theta) where it is largest.

components.purpose: Direct manipulation with a purpose: goals the learner reaches on the sliders. The controls stay locked until the prediction is made.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): MANIPULATE; meaningful direct manipulation

authoring.hint: manipulate.goals: each {prompt, goal: an expression true at the state to reach, hint}. Each goal must be reachable on the sliders' steps and not already met at the start; the check says if not.

components.purpose: The learner judges statements about what they saw; the page checks each against the whole model and shows a state that settles it.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): OBSERVE

authoring.hint: observe.statements: each {text, claim, truth, why}. claim is an expression checked at every state the sliders reach; truth says what that gives: always (a law of the model), never, or sometimes. Include at least one that is always true and the tempting one that is not. why explains it in a sentence.

components.purpose: The learner imposes the tempting model and sees, in the picture and on the graph, where it cannot be right, and why the correct model works.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): CONTRADICT; counterfactual requirement

authoring.hint: contradict: wrong_model {label, quantity} (the quantity that states the tempting model), imposes (one sentence: suppose the model were true), goal {prompt, goal, hint} (find a state where it visibly fails), why_correct and why_wrong (feedback must answer both why the correct model works and why the tempting one cannot). Show the tempting model in the scene with reveal: contradict, and as second_view.ghost.

components.purpose: Expose what is normally invisible, one cause at a time, in the order the cause acts.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): GRAPHICAL DECONSTRUCTION; G2 mechanism; explicit causal chain

authoring.hint: deconstruct.steps: each {text, reveals: [element ids], ask?: {prompt, options, correct, why}}; the elements it reveals have reveal: deconstruct in the scene and each is revealed by exactly one step. Order the steps as the causes act. A step may reveal nothing and only say what the last one means.

components.purpose: Build the mathematics from the visible mechanism: each step is a quantity the picture shows, and the final equation compresses them and is checked equal to the quantity at every state.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): MATHEMATICAL RECONSTRUCTION; the final equation is a compression of the visible mechanism

authoring.hint: reconstruct.steps: each {text, quantity} naming a quantity the mechanism showed; reconstruct.equation {text, expr}: the closed form that must equal the quantity the page is about at every state (the check says where it does not, and rejects an expression identical to the quantity's own).

components.purpose: The learner tries to break what survives every valid variation, and finds they cannot.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): INVARIANT DISCOVERY; representation invariants need an oracle

authoring.hint: invariants: each {text, lhs, rel, rhs, try}; rel is ==, <= or >=; the relation must hold at every state the sliders reach (the check says where it does not). try tells the learner how to look for a state that breaks it.

components.purpose: The learner finds where the shortcut stops being right: cases where it holds and cases where it fails, judged against the model.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): BOUNDARY STRESS

authoring.hint: boundary: assumption (what must hold for the shortcut), learner_must_identify (the point the learner takes away), cases: each {text, set: {parameter: value}, shortcut_label, shortcut: expression, expect: holds or fails}. The page compares the shortcut with the quantity the page is about at that state; expect must agree, and at least one case holds and one fails.

components.purpose: The supports are taken away in three levels: the numbers on the picture, then the relation, then the mechanism; the learner answers with less each time.
components.benchmark: GCDR v1.3 (docs/GRAPHICAL-COGNITIVE-DECONSTRUCTION-BLUEPRINT.md): SCAFFOLD FADE
